patch.value: Re-sharding the nightly matrix turns the reliability monitor red for weeks: renamed legs start at 0 attempts and fail insufficient_completed_attempts with no lineage to the legs they replaced

PR #1548 (e72f82813, 2026-10-22) re-partitioned nightly validation into 14 shard legs. The Release Reliability workflow (workflow_run) evaluates the rolling nightly window against the declared matrix population, so every new leg name (e.g. 'Nightly (ubuntu-latest, Node 24, shard 1/4)') has 0 completed attempts and reports insufficient_completed_attempts; the monitor exits 1 on every run until min_completed_attempts accrue per leg. The predecessor families ('Nightly (ubuntu-latest, Node 24)' 1/30 failed, etc.) still carry 30 attempts of history, but nothing declares that the shard legs REPLACE them. Empty families deliberately fail coverage (reliability.ts: empty families never masquerade as healthy), which is right, yet a red monitor for a known warm-up is indistinguishable from a real degradation and desensitises the alert. The same run also reports scheduled_failure_rate (5/30 original scheduled attempts) and dispatch_window violations for the release series.

A declared family lineage (successor legs name the family they replace) lets the evaluator report predecessor evidence for a renamed or re-sharded leg instead of 0/0; Warm-up (insufficient attempts on a leg younger than the window) is reported as a distinct non-failing state with its expiry date, while a real failure_rate violation on any leg still fails; The step summary separates coverage warm-up, failure-rate and dispatch findings with their owners; A negative control proves an undeclared rename (no lineage) still fails coverage; The SDK reliability window (src/sdk/governance/reliability.ts) owns the lineage and warm-up semantics, the collector only declares data

GITHUB_REPOSITORY=unbraind/pm-cli node --input-type=module -e 'import {main} from "./scripts/release/collect-nightly-reliability.mjs"; const r=main(); console.log(r.ok, r.families.map(f=>[f.family,f.completed,f.violations]))'
Re-sharding a matrix keeps the reliability monitor green unless a leg actually fails, and reports warm-up explicitly.
Release Reliability runs 39817294749 and 39817302614 (2026-10-22) exit 1: 14 renamed nightly legs report insufficient_completed_attempts at 0/0; macOS legs 1/3 failure_rate.
